chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Fadl, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Jamil, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, the One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What should be recited in the Friday prayer when traveling according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic principle of *ikhtisar* (shortening) in Friday prayer during travel, where reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas suffices for both rak'ahs. The text employs a logical deduction (*istidlal*) to argue that the Imam’s explicit authorization implies a normative legal status (wajib or mustahabb) rather than mere encouragement, as permitting a substitute for the full recitation suggests a binding concession. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of ritual law while maintaining the sanctity of the Friday prayer.
